Healthy: Leaves are healthy, no treatment required.
Early blight: May be early blight. It is recommended to promptly remove diseased leaves, avoid excessive humidity, and apply protective fungicides.
Late blight: May be late blight. Apply targeted fungicides in time and pay attention to field humidity control.
Leaf Mold: Leaf mold. Pay attention to temperature and humidity regulation, maintain ventilation, and spray fungicides when necessary.
Septoria leaf spot: May be Septoria leaf spot. Promptly remove diseased leaves and apply protective agents.
Two-spotted spider mite: May be caused by two-spotted spider mites. Pay attention to pest control.
Target Spot: Target spot. Avoid dense planting, strengthen ventilation, and use registered fungicides.
Tomato mosaic virus: Tomato mosaic virus. It is recommended to remove infected plants and ensure seed health.
Tomato yellow leaf curl virus: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus. Control the insect vectors (whiteflies) and remove infected plants.
Bacterial spot: Bacterial spot. Avoid excessive field humidity, and use copper-based chemicals or registered antibiotics when necessary.
